title: Personal Checking: savings balances in the Private Client Checking conversion test
content:
## Scope

This rule applies when an owner asks to convert an active Personal Checking account to Private Client Checking and the Relationship Balance is tested against the Private Client entry requirement. It states what the owner's PCB savings holdings contribute to that test.

## Formal clause

For this test, the savings contribution is the current balance of the owner's savings account in each of the statuses applied, active and dormant. The owner's savings balances in these counted statuses are a part of the Relationship Balance compared with the entry minimum.

## Counted statuses

| Owner's savings account status | Counted in the Private Client conversion test |
|---|---|
| Applied | Current balance counted |
| Active | Current balance counted |
| Dormant | Current balance counted |
| Any other status | Not counted |

## Worked cases (hypothetical owners)

- An owner has an active savings account holding 118000.00 USD. The savings contribution to the conversion test is 118000.00 USD.
- An owner has a dormant savings account holding 64000.00 USD. Dormant is counted, so 64000.00 USD enters the test.
- An owner's savings account was closed last year. A closed account is in none of the counted statuses and contributes nothing.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "only active savings accounts help an owner qualify". **Correct basis:** applied, active and dormant savings accounts are all counted.
